headline: Large Energy Users Pay Grid Costs
short_summary: This bill ensures large energy users, like data centers, bear the costs of their own grid infrastructure, preventing those costs from being passed to residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, Governor Spanberger's administration.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users.
news_headline: Virginia requires data centers to pay for their own power lines
news_summary: Virginia's State Corporation Commission ruled that data centers must pay the full cost for their required transmission infrastructure, preventing these billions of dollars in costs from falling on residential ratepayers. This decision, supported by Governor Spanberger, is expected to save Virginia residents hundreds of millions of dollars.

headline: Data Centers Report Water Usage
short_summary: This bill mandates data centers to report their water consumption, providing transparency and data for resource management.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local governments, water conservation advocates, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, championed by Senator Kannan Srinivasan, mandates local water authorities to report data center water usage, which will be publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This legislation aims to provide transparency regarding the significant water consumption by data centers, a growing industry in the state.

headline: Local Control Data Center Siting, Noise
short_summary: This bill grants local governments more authority over where data centers can be built and imposes limits on their operational noise, addressing community concerns.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups.
opponents: Data center developers, tech industry trade groups, chambers of commerce.
news_headline: Roanoke Delegate Helped Write Virginia's New Data Center Law
news_summary: A new Virginia law, HB 153, requires developers of large data centers to conduct site assessments examining noise impacts on nearby residential areas and schools. While it mandates studies and utility disclosures, the law does not set specific noise limits or water caps, empowering local governments with more information for siting decisions.
